answer: No cask leaves the dock without a bill of lading, signed by the merchant and sealed by the cellar master. A basalt cask shipped on a forged bill fails at the dock: the seal must be the master's own, checked at the mirror of the loading, and a cask with no bill is held on the quay. Forging a season of shipments means bribing the merchant, faking eighty bills and paying 20,700, while the lagoon book in the dock office is kept for the year, so a cask whose bill was never signed is confiscated.
